_comment: mono - no hue, but every icon keeps its own shipped brightness.
The colour half of this theme converts each TouchColors key to its Rec.709
luminance and changes nothing else, so that ordering, and therefore every
contrast relationship the interface depends on, survives untouched. The
icons follow exactly the same rule, and that is the entire recipe:
`grayscale` with amount 1.0 maps each pixel to its own luminance and
Deliberately no brightness or contrast op. Adding one here would be the
icon-side equivalent of the mistake the theme's own comments warn about -
flattening everything to one tone destroys the distinctions the icons use
to tell state apart (a dimmed `NoCook` badge versus a lit `Cook` one is
carried entirely by value, and there is no hue to fall back on).
The recipe therefore moves only 18 of the 97 icons, and that count is the
honest measure of the theme rather than a sign the recipe is too timid.
Desaturating a glyph that is already grey is a no-op by construction: 69
of the shipped icons are pure white with alpha and 3 are pure black, so 72
cannot change under a hue-removing op at all. The 18 that do move are the
genuinely coloured ones - the error and warning faces, the yellow star.
That is this theme working as intended, not an oversight.
